# CEO Review Working Plan: "Developer-friendly" pricing tier

Source: `PLAN.md:11-21` (reviewed plan). Skill: /plan-ceo-review. Branch: main. Date: 2026-10-18.

## Plan under review (verbatim scope, preserved)
- Goal: Increase developer adoption. (`PLAN.md:13-14`)
- Success metric: More signups. (`PLAN.md:16-17`)
- Premise: No developer has been asked whether current pricing is a barrier; team "feels like" it should be cheaper. (`PLAN.md:19-21`)

## Settled inputs (from user instructions, `CLAUDE.md` / `PLAN.md:1-7`)
- /office-hours prerequisite: skipped (user instruction).
- Routing setup, cross-project recall, outside reviewers: declined (user instruction).
- Review mode: HOLD SCOPE (user instruction). Product scope preserved.
- Review depth: strategy-only. The plan has no code, files or interfaces; the user asked for a plan review of a pricing/strategy change. Implementation detail stays as "implementation owner must prove ___".
- Landscape search: not run. Proceeding with in-distribution knowledge only.

## Pre-review system audit
- Repo contains only `CLAUDE.md` and `PLAN.md`; one commit (`e3ac2de Seed review plan`). No stashes, no TODOS.md, no TODO/FIXME markers, no design doc, no prior decisions, no learnings.
- No pricing code, billing system, analytics or funnel data exists in this repo to verify any claim. Every factual claim below is therefore unverified.

## Step 0A: Premise challenge
- **Stated problem:** developer adoption is lower than wanted.
- **Plan's remedy:** a cheaper tier.
- **Gap:** the plan admits (`PLAN.md:20-21`) nobody checked that price is the barrier. Developers commonly fail to adopt for other reasons: signup friction, time-to-first-success, docs quality, missing SDKs/integrations, no free trial/sandbox, procurement, or simply not knowing the product exists. A cheaper tier only fixes the price cause.
- **Proxy risk:** "More signups" (`PLAN.md:17`) is a proxy for adoption. A cheap tier can raise signups while activation, retention and revenue fall (cannibalization of existing paid plans).
- **Do-nothing cost:** unknown. No baseline adoption number is cited.
- **One-way-door note:** pricing cuts are hard to reverse. Raising a price later means grandfathering, churn and trust cost.

### Premise table (unverified=4)
| Premise | Claim | Receipt | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Developer adoption is too low | none (`PLAN.md:14` states goal, no baseline) | unverified |
| P2 | Current pricing is a barrier for developers | `PLAN.md:20-21` says untested | unverified (plan admits it) |
| P3 | A cheaper tier will raise adoption | none | unverified |
| P4 | More signups = more adoption | `PLAN.md:17`, no definition | unverified |

## Step 0B: Existing leverage
No code in repo. Reuse candidates are organizational: existing signup funnel analytics, pricing-page analytics, churn/cancel-reason surveys, sales/support tickets mentioning price. Implementation owner must prove which of these exist.

### Reality rows
- REALITY: premise-table finding 4 premises, unverified=4 PLAN.md:19
- REALITY: already-done pass no origin remote and single seed commit; nothing shipped PLAN.md:11
- REALITY: surface-check n/a-equivalent pass plan names no CLI commands, flags or routes PLAN.md:11
- REALITY: binding-decisions pass decision-search returned none; plan has no Binding decisions section PLAN.md:11
- REALITY: numbers finding plan cites no numbers; no baseline signups or target [re-measure before gate] PLAN.md:17
- REALITY: deferred-asks pass no linked issue PLAN.md:11
- REALITY: pr-count pass no .gstack/ship-policy.json; default one PR per wave, and plan is non-code PLAN.md:11

## Step 0C: Dream state
```
  CURRENT STATE                    THIS PLAN                       12-MONTH IDEAL
  Adoption "too low" (no      ---> Cheaper tier launched on   ---> Developers self-serve to first
  baseline); cause unknown;        gut feel; success = raw         success fast; pricing matches
  no developer interviews          signup count                    measured willingness to pay;
                                                                   adoption tracked as activation
                                                                   + retention, not signups
```
The plan moves toward the ideal only if price is in fact the barrier. If it is not, it spends a one-way pricing move and leaves the real cause untouched.

## Decision ledger
| ID and owner | Contract and evidence | Current | Proposed | Status | Exact approval and scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MODE (user) | CLAUDE.md instruction | HOLD SCOPE | n/a | approved | User instruction: "choose HOLD SCOPE (CEO)" |
| PREMISE-1 (plan owner) | `PLAN.md:19-21`: price-barrier premise untested | Launch tier on team intuition | A) launch as written; B) validation gate before launch; C) launch as a time-boxed experiment | unresolved | pending D1 |

## currentDecision (PREMISE-1)
Commitment comparison:
```text
Commitment                         | Source/approval      | Current        | A              | B                         | C
Launch developer tier (scope)      | PLAN.md:11, preserved| yes            | yes            | yes, after gate passes    | yes, to a cohort
Evidence before pricing commitment | pending              | none           | none           | 10-15 dev interviews +    | live A/B result
                                   |                      |                |                | funnel drop-off analysis  |
Reversibility of price move        | pending              | low            | low            | low, but decided on data  | high during test window
Time to launch                     | pending              | now            | now            | +~2 weeks                 | now, decision in ~4-6 wks
Success metric definition          | separate row (later) | "more signups" | unchanged here | unchanged here            | unchanged here
```

Question: D1 — PREMISE-1: Should the tier launch on the untested "pricing is the barrier" premise? Project: PLAN.md on main proposes a cheaper developer tier. ELI10: The team wants to make a cheaper plan for developers, but nobody has asked developers if price is what stops them. If the real blocker is something else (hard signup, bad docs), a cheaper plan won't help and price cuts are hard to undo. Stakes: we cut price, lose revenue from people who would have paid more, and adoption stays flat. Recommendation: B because a two-week check is cheap compared to a price cut you can't easily take back. Note: options differ in kind, not coverage; no completeness score. Net: speed of launch versus confidence that the launch fixes the real problem.
Header: Premise
A) Launch as written
Ship the tier now on team intuition. Effort S (zero extra work), risk high, no verification. ✅ Fastest path; the tier exists within the current timeline and plan text stays unchanged. ✅ Zero added discovery work or research cost before the team can start building. ❌ If price is not the barrier, revenue drops and adoption stays flat, and the cut is hard to reverse.
B) Validate first (recommended)
Gate the launch on 10-15 developer interviews plus pricing-page and signup funnel drop-off analysis; launch only if price shows up as a top barrier. Effort M (human ~2 weeks / CC ~1 day to draft scripts and queries), risk low. ✅ Tier stays in scope; it just ships on evidence instead of a feeling. ✅ If the real barrier is elsewhere, the team learns it before spending a one-way pricing move. ❌ Delays launch about two weeks and needs someone to own the interviews.
C) Launch as a time-boxed experiment
Offer the tier to a random cohort of new visitors for 4-6 weeks with a pre-declared success bar, then keep or kill. Effort L, risk medium. ✅ Measures real behavior, not stated preferences, so it catches what interviews miss. ✅ Reversible during the window because only a cohort sees the price. ❌ Needs billing support for cohort pricing and enough traffic for a readable result.
